title: App Configuration Feature Flags and Labels
description: Learn how to use feature flags for gradual rollouts and labels for environment-specific configuration.

data.text: Feature flags let you turn features on or off without deploying new code. You can roll out a feature to 10% of users, then 50%, then 100%, all from App Configuration.

Labels in App Configuration let you store different values for the same key in different environments. For example, 'ApiUrl' might point to a local API in 'development' and a cloud API in 'production'.

data.title: Feature Flag Patterns
items: On/Off — enable a feature for everyone or no one
Percentage rollout — gradually enable for a percentage of users
Targeting — enable for specific users, groups, or devices
Time-based — enable after a specific date

data.title: Create a Feature Flag
data.content: Add a feature flag named 'BetaCheckout' and set it to true.
data.code: az appconfig feature set   --name myAppConfig   --feature BetaCheckout   --enable true

data.title: Add a Labeled Key-Value
data.content: Store different API URLs for dev and production environments.
data.code:
# Development
az appconfig kv set   --name myAppConfig   --key "ApiUrl"   --value "https://dev-api.example.com"   --label "development"

# Production
az appconfig kv set   --name myAppConfig   --key "ApiUrl"   --value "https://api.example.com"   --label "production"

data.caption: How feature flags and labels let you target different environments.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    AppConfig["App Configuration"] -->|"Key: ApiUrl, Label: development"| Dev["Development App"]
    AppConfig -->|"Key: ApiUrl, Label: production"| Prod["Production App"]
    AppConfig -->|"Feature: BetaCheckout = true"| Beta["Beta Users Only"]

data.text: A feature flag is only useful if the application can evaluate it without a redeploy. The Microsoft.FeatureManagement library reads flags from configuration (including App Configuration) and evaluates filters such as percentage rollout or targeting. The flag name is a key with the prefix .appconfig.featureflag/, and the value is a JSON document describing the state and filters.

data.title: Evaluate a flag in an ASP.NET Core endpoint
data.content: Register feature management, then inject IFeatureManager. The provider refresh interval decides how quickly a change is picked up.

data.title: Add a percentage filter from the CLI
data.content: The Microsoft.Percentage filter enables the flag for a stable percentage of users. Targeting filters can key on user ID, group, or custom attributes.
data.code:
az appconfig feature filter add \
  --name shop-appconfig \
  --feature BetaCheckout \
  --filter-name Microsoft.Percentage \
  --filter-parameters Percentage=10

# Enable the flag and confirm its filters
az appconfig feature set --name shop-appconfig --feature BetaCheckout --enable true
az appconfig feature show --name shop-appconfig --feature BetaCheckout -o json

data.title: Rules for safe feature flags
items: Give every flag an owner and an expiry date; stale flags become permanent branches in production.
Never treat a flag as authorization. A user can still call the endpoint directly, so enforce permissions server-side.
Log the evaluated variant with the request so you can correlate errors with a rollout.
Use labels or separate stores for environment-specific flag state, and keep production flags out of development experiments.
Remove the flag and the dead branch once the rollout reaches 100%.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Feature flags decouple deployment from release. That is the sentence to lead with. Then distinguish release flags (short-lived) from operational kill switches (long-lived) and experiment flags (need assignment and analysis), and mention that flags add branching and test-matrix cost.

data.title: Implement a Feature Flag
data.description: Create a feature flag that controls whether a welcome banner is shown, then test toggling it.
steps: Add it to your app using the App Configuration provider.
Toggle the flag on and off in the Azure Portal.
Refresh your app and observe the banner change without redeploying.
data.expectedOutcome: The banner appears or disappears based on the feature flag value.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Feature flags decouple deployment from release.
Labels let one key hold multiple environment values.
App Configuration providers automatically refresh values when they change.
